sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sa rājā krodhamūrchitaḥ vāsaviṃ navabhir bāṇair bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Then, taking up another bow, that king, beside himself with rage, struck the son of Vāsava with nine arrows in the arms and in the breast.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaḥ smayann eva śrutāyudham ariṃdamaḥ śarair anekasāhasraiḥ pīḍayām āsa bhārata
english: Then Arjuna, tamer of foes, smiling all the while, harried Śrutāyudha with many thousands of arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: aśvāṃś cāsyāvadhīt tūrṇaṃ sārathiṃ ca mahārathaḥ vivyādha cainaṃ saptatyā nārācānāṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Swiftly the great chariot-warrior slew his horses and his charioteer, and that mighty one pierced him with seventy iron shafts.

sanskrit: hatāśvaṃ ratham utsṛjya sa tu rājā śrutāyudhaḥ abhyadravad raṇe pārthaṃ gadām udyamya vīryavān
english: Abandoning his chariot, its horses slain, that valiant king Śrutāyudha rushed upon Pārtha in battle, lifting high his mace.

sanskrit: varuṇasyātmajo vīraḥ sa tu rājā śrutāyudhaḥ parṇāśā jananī yasya śītatoyā mahānadī
english: That heroic king Śrutāyudha was the son of Varuṇa, and his mother was Parṇāśā, the great river of cool waters.

sanskrit: tasya mātābravīd vākyaṃ varuṇaṃ putrakāraṇāt avadhyo 'yaṃ bhavelloke śatrūṇāṃ tanayo mama
english: For her son's sake his mother once spoke these words to Varuṇa: 'May this son of mine become unslayable by his enemies in the world.'

sanskrit: varuṇas tv abravīt prīto dadāmy asmai varaṃ hitam divyam astraṃ sutas te 'yaṃ yanāvadhyo bhaviṣyati
english: And Varuṇa, well pleased, replied: 'I grant him a boon for his welfare—a divine weapon, by which this son of yours shall be unslayable.'

sanskrit: nāsti cāpy amaratvaṃ vai manuṣyasya kathaṃ cana sarveṇāvaśyamartavyaṃ jātena saritāṃ vare
english: 'Yet immortality is in no wise possible for a mortal; whoever is born, O best of rivers, must of necessity die.'

sanskrit: durdharṣas tv eṣa śatrūṇāṃ raṇeṣu bhavitā sadā astrasyāsya prabhāvād vai vyetu te mānaso jvaraḥ
english: 'But through the power of this weapon he shall always be unassailable by his foes in battle; let the fever of your heart depart.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā varuṇaḥ prādād gadāṃ mantrapuraskṛtām yām āsādya durādharṣaḥ sarvaloke śrutāyudhaḥ
english: So saying, Varuṇa bestowed a mace consecrated with sacred spells, by gaining which Śrutāyudha became unassailable in all the world.

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ bhagavān punar eva jaleśvaraḥ ayudhyati na moktavyā sā tvayy eva pated iti
english: And the lord of the waters spoke to him once more: 'It must not be loosed against one who does not fight; else it shall fall back upon you yourself.'

sanskrit: sa tayā vīraghātinyā janārdanam atāḍayat pratijagrāha tāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pīnenāṃsena vīryavān
english: With that hero-slaying mace he smote Janārdana; but the valiant Kṛṣṇa received it upon his broad shoulder.

sanskrit: nākampayata śauriṃ sā vindhyaṃ girim ivānilaḥ pratyabhyayāt taṃ viproḍhā kṛtyeva duradhiṣṭhitā
english: It did not shake the scion of Śūra, as the wind cannot shake the Vindhya mountain; flung back, it returned upon its own caster like an ill-conjured spell of witchcraft.

sanskrit: jaghāna cāsthitaṃ vīraṃ śrutāyudham amarṣaṇam hatvā śrutāyudhaṃ vīraṃ jagatīm anvapadyata
english: It struck down the wrathful hero Śrutāyudha as he stood there; and having slain the hero Śrutāyudha, it fell to the earth.

sanskrit: hāhākāro mahāṃs tatra sainyānāṃ samajāyata svenāstreṇa hataṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutāyudham ariṃdamam
english: A great cry of dismay rose up among the troops there, when they saw Śrutāyudha, that tamer of foes, slain by his own weapon.

sanskrit: ayudhyamānāya hi sā keśavāya narādhipa kṣiptā śrutāyudhenātha tasmāt tam avadhīd gadā
english: For it had been hurled by Śrutāyudha at Keśava, who was not then fighting, O lord of men; and therefore the mace slew him.

sanskrit: yathoktaṃ varuṇenājau tathā sa nidhanaṃ gataḥ vyasuś cāpy apatad bhūmau prekṣatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: Even as Varuṇa had foretold, so did he meet his death in battle; and lifeless he fell to the ground before the eyes of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: patamānas tu sa babhau parṇāśāyāḥ priyaḥ sutaḥ saṃbhagna iva vātena bahuśākho vanaspatiḥ
english: As he fell, that dear son of Parṇāśā shone like a many-branched forest tree shattered by the wind.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇi sainyāni senāmukhyāś ca sarvaśaḥ prādravanta hataṃ dṛṣṭvā śrutāyudham ariṃdamam
english: Then all the troops, and the leaders of the host on every side, took to flight when they saw Śrutāyudha, tamer of foes, slain.

sanskrit: tatha kāmbojarājasya putraḥ śūraḥ sudakṣiṇaḥ abhyayāj javanair aśvaiḥ phalgunaṃ śatrusūdanam
english: Then the brave Sudakṣiṇa, son of the king of the Kāmbojas, advanced with swift horses against Phalguna, slayer of foes.

sanskrit: tasya pārthaḥ śarān sapta preṣayām āsa bhārata te taṃ śūraṃ vinirbhidya prāviśan dharaṇītalam
english: Pārtha loosed seven arrows at him, O Bhārata; piercing through that hero, they sank into the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: so 'tividdhaḥ śarais tīkṣṇair gāṇḍīvapreṣitair mṛdhe arjunaṃ prativivyādha daśabhiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Sorely wounded in the fray by the sharp shafts sped from the Gāṇḍīva, he pierced Arjuna in return with ten heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: vāsudevaṃ tribhir viddhvā punaḥ pārthaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ tasya pārtho dhanuś chittvā ketuṃ ciccheda māriṣa
english: Having pierced Vāsudeva with three shafts and Pārtha again with five, Pārtha then cut apart his bow and severed his banner, O sire.

sanskrit: bhallābhyāṃ bhṛśatīkṣṇābhyāṃ taṃ ca vivyādha pāṇḍavaḥ sa tu pārthaṃ tribhir viddhvā siṃhanādam athānadat
english: The Pāṇḍava pierced him with two exceedingly keen broad-headed shafts; but he, having struck Pārtha with three, sent forth a lion's roar.

sanskrit: sarvapāraśavīṃ caiva śaktiṃ śūraḥ sudakṣiṇaḥ saghaṇṭāṃ prāhiṇod ghorāṃ kruddho gāṇḍīvadhanvane
english: And the brave Sudakṣiṇa, in his wrath, hurled at the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva a dreadful all-iron lance hung with bells.

sanskrit: sā jvalantī maholkeva tam āsādya mahāratham savisphuliṅgā nirbhidya nipapāta mahītale
english: Blazing like a great meteor, scattering sparks, it reached that mighty chariot-warrior, pierced through, and fell upon the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ caturdaśabhiḥ pārtho nārācaiḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ sāśvadhvajadhanuḥsūtaṃ vivyādhācintyavikramaḥ rathaṃ cānyaiḥ subahubhiś cakre viśakalaṃ śaraiḥ
english: With fourteen heron-feathered iron shafts Pārtha of inconceivable prowess pierced him together with his horses, banner, bow, and charioteer, and with many other arrows shattered his chariot to pieces.

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇaṃ tu kāmbojaṃ moghasaṃkalpavikramam bibheda hṛdi bāṇena pṛthudhāreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍava pierced through the heart of Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja—his resolve and prowess now brought to naught—with a broad-bladed arrow.

sanskrit: sa bhinnamarmā srastāṅgaḥ prabhraṣṭamukuṭāṅgadaḥ papātābhimukhaḥ śūro yantramukta iva dhvajaḥ
english: His vital parts pierced, his limbs gone slack, his crown and armlets fallen away, that hero pitched forward like a banner released from its pole.

sanskrit: gireḥ śikharajaḥ śrīmān suśākhaḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ nirbhagna iva vātena karṇikāro himātyaye
english: He was like a lovely karṇikāra tree, fair-branched and firmly rooted, born upon a mountain summit, broken down by the wind at winter's end.

sanskrit: śete sma nihato bhūmau kāmbojāstaraṇocitaḥ sudarśanīyas tāmrākṣaḥ karṇinā sa sudakṣiṇaḥ putraḥ kāmbojarājasya pārthena vinipātitaḥ
english: Slain, he lay upon the bare ground—he who had been used to Kāmboja coverlets—fair to look upon, copper-eyed: that Sudakṣiṇa, son of the king of the Kāmbojas, struck down by Pārtha with a barbed shaft.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇi sainyāni vyadravanta sutasya te hataṃ śrutāyudhaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmbojaṃ ca sudakṣiṇam
english: Then all the troops of your son took to flight, seeing Śrutāyudha slain and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja as well.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hate sudakṣiṇe rājan vīre caiva śrutāyudhe javenābhyadravan pārthaṃ kupitāḥ sainikās tava
english: Saṃjaya said: When Sudakṣiṇa was slain, O king, and the hero Śrutāyudha as well, your soldiers in fury rushed swiftly upon Pārtha.

sanskrit: abhīṣāhāḥ śūrasenāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ abhyavarṣaṃs tato rājañ śaravarṣair dhanaṃjayam
english: The Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Śibis, and the Vasātis then rained showers of arrows upon Dhanaṃjaya, O king.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ṣaṣṭiśatānāryān prāmathnāt pāṇḍavaḥ śaraiḥ te sma bhītāḥ palāyanta vyāghrāt kṣudramṛgā iva
english: The Pāṇḍava crushed six thousand of those noble warriors with his arrows, and in terror they fled, like small deer before a tiger.

sanskrit: te nivṛtya punaḥ pārthaṃ sarvataḥ paryavārayan raṇe sapatnān nighnantaṃ jigīṣantan parān yudhi
english: Turning back again, they hemmed Pārtha in on every side as he slew his adversaries in the fray and sought to conquer his foes in battle.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ tūrṇaṃ gāṇḍīvapreṣitaiḥ śaraiḥ śirāṃsi pātayām āsa bāhūṃś caiva dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: As they swiftly bore down upon him, Dhanaṃjaya struck off their heads and their arms with arrows sped from the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: śirobhiḥ patitais tatra bhūmir āsīn nirantarā abhracchāyeva caivāsīd dhvāṅkṣagṛdhravaḍairyudhi
english: The ground there was packed close with fallen heads, and the battlefield grew dark, as if shadowed by clouds, with crows, vultures, and kites.

sanskrit: teṣu tūtsādyamāneṣu krodhāmarṣasamanvitau śrutāyuś cācyutāyuś ca dhanaṃjayam ayudhyatām
english: While they were being cut down, Śrutāyu and Acyutāyu, filled with wrath and indignation, fought against Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: balinau spardhinau vīrau kulajau bāhuśālinau tāv enaṃ śaravarṣāṇi savyadakṣiṇam asyatām
english: Those two heroes, strong, emulous, nobly born, and mighty of arm, poured showers of arrows upon him from the left and from the right.

sanskrit: tvarāyuktau mahārāja prārthayānau mahad yaśaḥ arjunasya vadhaprepsū putrārthe tava dhanvinau
english: Both swift, O great king, both seeking great renown and bent on Arjuna's slaying, those two bowmen fought for your son's sake.

sanskrit: tāv arjunaṃ sahasreṇa patriṇāṃ nataparvaṇām pūrayām āsatuḥ kruddhau taḍāgaṃ jaladau yathā
english: In their wrath the two of them covered Arjuna with a thousand smooth-jointed feathered shafts, as rain-clouds fill a tank with water.

sanskrit: śrutāyuś ca tataḥ kruddhas tomareṇa dhanaṃjayam ājaghāna rathaśreṣṭhaḥ pītena niśitena ca
english: Then the wrathful Śrutāyu, foremost of chariot-warriors, struck Dhanaṃjaya with a sharp, gold-burnished lance.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā śatruṇā śatrukarśanaḥ ājagāma paraṃ mohaṃ mohayan keśavaṃ raṇe
english: Sorely wounded by his mighty foe, that scourge of his enemies sank into a deep swoon, dismaying Keśava in the battle.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu so 'cyutāyur mahārathaḥ śūlena bhṛśatīkṣṇena tāḍayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: At that very moment the great chariot-warrior Acyutāyu smote the Pāṇḍava with an exceedingly sharp spear.

sanskrit: kṣate kṣāraṃ sa hi dadau pāṇḍavasya mahātmanaḥ pārtho 'pi bhṛśasaṃviddho dhvajayaṣṭiṃ samāśritaḥ
english: He thus rubbed salt into the wound of the high-souled Pāṇḍava; and Pārtha, grievously stricken, leaned upon his banner-staff.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvasya sainyasya tāvakasya viśāṃ pate siṃhanādo mahān āsīd dhataṃ matvā dhanaṃjayam
english: Then from all your host, O lord of peoples, there rose a great lion's roar, for they thought Dhanaṃjaya slain.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaś ca bhṛśasaṃtapto dṛṣṭvā pārthaṃ vicetasam āśvāsayat suhṛdyābhir vāgbhis tatra dhanaṃjayam
english: And Kṛṣṇa, sore distressed to see Pārtha senseless, comforted Dhanaṃjaya there with kindly, heartening words.

sanskrit: tatas tau rathināṃ śreṣṭhau labdhalakṣau dhanaṃjayam vāsudevaṃ ca vārṣṇeyaṃ śaravarṣaiḥ samantataḥ
english: Then those two foremost of chariot-warriors, finding their mark, beset Dhanaṃjaya and Vāsudeva of the Vṛṣṇis with showers of arrows on every side.

sanskrit: sacakrakūbararathaṃ sāśvadhvajapatākinam adṛśyaṃ cakratur yuddhe tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: They made the chariot, with its wheels and yoke-pole, its horses, banner, and pennon, invisible in the fray—a thing that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: pratyāśvastas tu bībhatsuḥ śanakair iva bhārata pretarājapuraṃ prāpya punaḥ pratyāgato yathā
english: But Bībhatsu, recovering little by little, O Bhārata, was as one who had reached the city of the king of the dead and come back again.

sanskrit: saṃchannaṃ śarajālena rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā sakeśavam śatrū cābhimukhau dṛṣṭvā dīpyamānāv ivānalau
english: Seeing his chariot, with Keśava upon it, shrouded in a net of arrows, and seeing his two foes confronting him, blazing like fires,

sanskrit: prāduścakre tataḥ pārthaḥ śākram astraṃ mahārathaḥ tasmād āsan sahasrāṇi śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām
english: the great chariot-warrior Pārtha then brought forth the weapon of Indra, and from it came thousands of smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: te jaghnus tau maheṣvāsau tābhyāṃ sṛṣṭāṃś ca sāyakān vicerur ākāśagatāḥ pārthabāṇavidāritāḥ
english: These struck down both those great archers, and the shafts loosed by the two of them, riven by Pārtha's arrows, scattered through the sky.

sanskrit: pratihatya śarāṃs tūrṇaṃ śaravegena pāṇḍavaḥ pratasthe tatra tatraiva yodhayan vai mahārathān
english: Having swiftly beaten back their arrows by the speed of his own, the Pāṇḍava pressed on here and there, doing battle with the great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: tau ca phalgunabāṇaughair vibāhuśirasau kṛtau vasudhām anvapadyetāṃ vātanunnāv iva drumau
english: And those two, their arms and heads shorn away by the floods of Phalguna's arrows, sank to the earth like trees felled by the wind.

sanskrit: śrutāyuṣaś ca nidhanaṃ vadhaś caivācyutāyuṣaḥ lokavismāpanam abhūt samudrasyeva śoṣaṇam
english: The death of Śrutāyu and the slaying of Acyutāyu astonished the world, like the drying up of the ocean.

sanskrit: tayoḥ padānugān hatvā punaḥ pañcaśatān rathān abhyagād bhāratīṃ senāṃ nighnan pārtho varān varān
english: Having slain their followers, and five hundred chariots besides, Pārtha advanced upon the Bhārata host, striking down the noblest of the noble.

sanskrit: śrutāyuṣaṃ ca nihataṃ prekṣya caivācyutāyuṣam ayutāyuś ca saṃkruddho dīrghāyuś caiva bhārata
english: Beholding Śrutāyu slain and Acyutāyu likewise, Ayutāyu and Dīrghāyu were filled with wrath, O Bhārata—

sanskrit: putrau tayor naraśreṣṭhau kaunteyaṃ pratijagmatuḥ kirantau vividhān bāṇān pitṛvyasanakarśitau
english: the two sons of those slain heroes, best of men, advanced against the son of Kuntī, pouring forth arrows of every kind, sore stricken by their fathers' fall.

sanskrit: tāv arjuno muhūrtena śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ preṣayat paramakruddho yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: In an instant Arjuna, in his utmost wrath, dispatched the two of them with smooth-jointed arrows to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: loḍayantam anīkāni dvipaṃ padmasaro yathā nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ pārthaṃ kṣatriyapuṃgavāḥ
english: As he churned the hostile ranks like an elephant churning a lotus-pool, the bull-like warriors could not check Pārtha.

sanskrit: aṅgās tu gajavāreṇa pāṇḍavaṃ paryavārayan kruddhāḥ sahasraśo rājañ śikhitā hastisādinaḥ
english: But the Aṅgas, wrathful and crested with plumes, hemmed in the Pāṇḍava with a host of elephants, by thousands, O king—those riders of elephants.

sanskrit: duryodhanasamādiṣṭāḥ kuñjaraiḥ parvatopamaiḥ prācyāś ca dākṣiṇātyāś ca kaliṅgapramukhā nṛpāḥ
english: At Duryodhana's command came the kings of the East and the South, with the Kaliṅgas at their head, mounted on elephants like mountains.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ śīghraṃ gāṇḍīvapreṣitaiḥ śaraiḥ nicakarta śirāṃsy ugrau bāhūn api subhūṣaṇān
english: As they swiftly bore down upon him, with arrows sped from the Gāṇḍīva he fiercely lopped off their heads and their well-adorned arms.

sanskrit: taiḥ śirobhir mahī kīrṇā bāhubhiś ca sahāṅgadaiḥ babhau kanakapāṣāṇā bhujagair iva saṃvṛtā
english: The earth, strewn with those heads and with arms still wearing their armlets, gleamed like a field of golden boulders overspread with serpents.

sanskrit: bāhavo viśikhaiś chinnāḥ śirāṃsy unmathitāni ca cyavamānāny adṛśyanta drumebhya iva pakṣiṇaḥ
english: Arms cut off by his shafts, and heads struck away, were seen falling like birds tumbling down from trees.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ sahasraśo viddhā dvipāḥ prasrutaśoṇitāḥ vyadṛśyantādrayaḥ kāle gairikāmbusravā iva
english: The elephants, pierced by arrows in their thousands and streaming blood, looked like mountains in the rainy season pouring down red ochre-tinged water.

sanskrit: nihatāḥ śerate smānye bībhatsor niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ gajapṛṣṭhagatā mlecchā nānāvikṛtadarśanāḥ
english: Others lay slain by Bībhatsu's keen shafts—barbarians mounted upon the elephants' backs, of strange and misshapen aspect.

sanskrit: nānāveṣadharā rājan nānāśastraughasaṃvṛtāḥ rudhireṇānuliptāṅgā bhānti citraiḥ śarair hatāḥ
english: In varied garb, O king, surrounded by floods of varied weapons, their limbs smeared with blood, they shone—slain by his many-hued arrows.

sanskrit: śoṇitaṃ nirvamanti sma dvipāḥ pārthaśarāhatāḥ sahasraśaś chinnagātrāḥ sārohāḥ sapadānugāḥ
english: The elephants, struck by Pārtha's arrows, vomited forth blood by the thousand, their bodies torn, together with their riders and their attendants.

sanskrit: cukruśuś ca nipetuś ca babhramuś cāpare diśaḥ bhṛśaṃ trastāś ca bahudhā svānena mamṛdur gajāḥ sāntarāyudhikā mattā dvipās tīkṣṇaviṣopamāḥ
english: They shrieked and fell, while others wandered off in every direction; and greatly terrified, the maddened elephants, like sharp venom themselves, with the fighters mounted upon them, in their panic crushed many of their own by their trampling rush.

sanskrit: vidanty asuramāyāṃ ye sughorā ghoracakṣuṣaḥ yavanāḥ pāradāś caiva śakāś ca sunikaiḥ saha
english: Those most dreadful, grim-eyed ones who know the wizardry of the Asuras—the Yavanas, the Pāradas, the Śakas together with the Sunikas,

sanskrit: goyoniprabhavā mlecchāḥ kālakalpāḥ prahāriṇaḥ dārvābhisārā daradāḥ puṇḍrāś ca saha bāhlikaiḥ
english: the barbarians sprung of cattle, smiters fierce as Death himself, the Dārvābhisāras, the Daradas, and the Puṇḍras together with the Bāhlikas—

sanskrit: na te sma śakyāḥ saṃkhyātuṃ vrātāḥ śatasahasraśaḥ vṛṣṭis tathāvidhā hy āsīc chalabhānām ivāyatiḥ
english: those throngs, in their hundreds of thousands, could not be numbered; and such was the storm of their shafts, like an onrush of locusts.

sanskrit: abhracchāyām iva śaraiḥ sainye kṛtvā dhanaṃjayaḥ muṇḍārdhamuṇḍajaṭilān aśucīñ jaṭilānanān mlecchān aśātayat sarvān sametān astramāyayā
english: Casting over the host with his arrows a shadow as of clouds, Dhanaṃjaya, by the magic of his weapons, cut down all those barbarians gathered there—the shaven, the half-shaven, the matted-haired, the unclean, the shaggy-faced.

sanskrit: śaraiś ca śataśo viddhās te saṃghāḥ saṃghacāriṇaḥ prādravanta raṇe bhītā girigahvaravāsinaḥ
english: Pierced by arrows in their hundreds, those bands that moved in bands fled in terror from the field—dwellers of mountain caverns.

sanskrit: gajāśvasādimlecchānāṃ patitānāṃ śataiḥ śaraiḥ vaḍāḥ kaṅkā vṛkā bhūmāv apiban rudhiraṃ mudā
english: From the elephants, horses, riders, and barbarians fallen by his hundreds of arrows, the kites, the herons, and the wolves drank the blood upon the ground with joy.

sanskrit: pattyaśvarathanāgaiś ca pracchannakṛtasaṃkramām śaravarṣaplavāṃ ghorāṃ keśaśaivalaśāḍvalām prāvartayan nadīm ugrāṃ śoṇitaughataraṅgiṇīm
english: With footmen, horses, chariots, and elephants for its hidden fords, with showers of arrows for its rafts, dreadful, its weeds and grasses the hair of the slain, he set flowing a terrible river that surged with tides of blood.

sanskrit: śirastrāṇakṣudramatsyāṃ yugānte kālasaṃbhṛtām akarod gajasaṃbādhāṃ nadīm uttaraśoṇitām dehebhyo rājaputrāṇāṃ nāgāśvarathasādinām
english: With helmets for its little fish, gathered up by Time as at the end of an age, choked with elephants, he made a river overflowing with blood—drawn from the bodies of princes and of the riders of elephants, horses, and chariots.
